correctness.rationale: All perfect matchings are recursively and exhaustively generated (42), their disjoint triples generate exactly all 20 proper unlabelled edge colorings; all color-pair alternating cycles are exhaustively flipped. The complete 20-row adjacency certificate has two 10-vertex components, each with one universal node and three leaf triangles. A separately coded direct edge-color assignment enumerator obtains the identical 20-coloring / 36-edge graph digest. The proof relies on finite exhaustive coverage, not sampling or extending beyond the one fixed graph.

The 2021 algorithm determines components while suppressing root-cycle flips; its aggregate tables provide only class counts and do not assert the Pappus windmill structure. Crossed prisms of order divisible by four are not the eighteen-vertex Pappus graph.

evidence: Proposition 2.1 of Belcastro–Haas (2017) shows the graph of all *named* colorings is triangle-free, whereas the different color-permutation quotient computed here has triangles; there is no contradiction.
Goedgebeur–Östergård (2021) reports class counts, not the twenty-vertex graph with components containing degree-nine and degree-three vertices.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact structural claim does not follow from generic quotient definitions, a connectivity class count, or the published crossed-prism theorem without computing the Pappus-specific colorings and every quotient flip. In particular, the root-fixed graph used in 2017 is a spanning subgraph and cannot be equated with this quotient; the 2021 algorithm ignores root cycles for counting connected components, not for preserving all exchange edges. The reproducible certificate establishes the complete quotient. Absolute publication priority remains open.

evidence: Belcastro–Haas (2017) §2.2 specifies one representative per color-name orbit for KE_v but only allows switches preserving the colors incident at the chosen vertex; it does not identify its edge set with the full color-permutation quotient.
Goedgebeur–Östergård (2021) Algorithm 1 omits switches on cycles through a chosen vertex because this omission preserves *Kempe equivalence classes*, not individual adjacency.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The full quotient and the vertex-fixed graph correspond bijectively on coloring configurations, but their edge sets can differ. A flip on a two-color cycle through the root can be restored to the root normalization by globally transposing its colors; in a three-cycle two-factor this is equivalent to flipping the OTHER TWO cycles simultaneously, which need not be an edge of the root-fixed graph. Thus the quotient can contain triangles, whereas the fully named graph and its root-fixed subgraph are triangle-free. Earlier methods for equivalence-class counting can discard root-cycle switches without preserving every quotient edge. The present complete Pappus quotient edge structure has no identified statement-level coverage.

value.rationale: Kempe-move connectivity of a canonical nonplanar highly symmetric cubic bipartite graph is a motivated structural reconfiguration question. The result gives full adjacency and topology of each class, quantitative local mobility (degree 9 versus 3), exact exchange distances, and a cycle-structure characterization of the central configurations; these are not given by a bare equivalence class count.
